documents.title: Generative AI Syllabus Statement Considerations
tiers: No use of generative AI permitted
Use permitted under some circumstances or with explicit permission
documents.summary: CTE guidance offering three institutional options for AI syllabus statements and recommending a hybrid: a minimum-syllabus addition requiring instructors and students to set expectations and tying AI use to the Aggie Honor Code. Most of the text is sample statements from other universities, grouped into three permission levels.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule. It recommends a hybrid in which instructors and students "establish clear expectations for generative AI use within each course and/or assignment", and its samples come in three permission-level tiers that are "not institutional policies", so the stance is delegates.

units.why: Framing sentence: the university wants to approach generative AI with "scholarly rigor, intellectual integrity, and educational excellence"; a statement of purpose and principle, so P56.
units.anchor: Texas A&M University wishes to approach the introduction of generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) with

units.why: Says AI brings "additional challenges to academic integrity" and "stimulating opportunities to educate effectively for the future of learning and work"; the work-preparation half is P44, and the integrity half is in fit_note.
units.anchor: The university recognizes that generative AI presents additional challenges to academic integrity and simultaneously presents
units.fit_note: Also names academic-integrity challenges; the unit is a balanced rationale.

units.why: Option 1 of three courses of action: a university-wide syllabus statement "added to minimum syllabus requirements"; it is a syllabus-statement requirement (P09), but only an option, hence informs.
units.anchor: syllabus statement to be added to minimum syllabus requirements
units.fit_note: Presented as one option considered, not an adopted rule.

units.why: Option 2: "allow individual instructors to determine their own syllabus statement"; the decision rests with each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: allow individual instructors to determine their own syllabus statement identifying acceptable use of generative AI

units.why: The recommended hybrid adds to minimum syllabus requirements the "responsibility of instructors and students to establish clear expectations" per course or assignment; chose P09 (syllabus requirement) over P04 because it mandates stating expectations.
units.anchor: establish clear expectations for generative AI use within each course and/or assignment

units.why: The recommended addition "reinforces that the use of generative AI in academic coursework is integrally related to academic integrity and will be governed by the Aggie Honor Code"; AI misuse handled under existing integrity rules, P36.
units.anchor: will be governed by the Aggie Honor Code

units.why: "Guidance provided to support faculty in making their individual determinations" is the second element of the recommended option; support for faculty setting course policy, P63.
units.anchor: Guidance provided to support faculty in making their individual determinations

documents.unit: Texas A&M AI initiative / Division of Academic Affairs
documents.title: Use Guidelines and Ethics (Teach with AI)
documents.summary: University AI site page giving ethical principles and role-based best practices for faculty, staff and students. For academic work it asks for cited AI use, allows spelling/grammar help but not new text, and leaves course-level rules to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The page says "The faculty should provide clear instructions about permissible AI uses in their courses" and that professors can require AI per syllabus, while setting shared principles; it does not itself fix a stance, so delegates.

units.why: Purpose: guidance on "responsible use of generative AI" while "minimizing risks to academic integrity, privacy and other ethical use considerations"; institution-level framework, P56.
units.anchor: recommendations and guidance on the responsible use of generative AI at Texas A & M

units.why: "Generative AI use ... should adhere to the same ethical principles ... including privacy, fairness, transparency, bias, and accountability"; a principles framework, P56.
units.anchor: should adhere to the same ethical principles used in other aspects of education, research, and

units.why: "conduct routine audits to detect and address prejudices"; auditing AI systems for bias, P98.
units.anchor: conduct routine audits to detect and address prejudices

units.why: "Everyone should ensure the AI systems are transparent and explainable to professors and students"; closest to P103 (people should understand the AI they deal with).
units.anchor: AI systems are transparent and explainable to professors and students
units.fit_note: About transparency and explainability of systems, not telling people they face an AI.

units.why: "Everyone must follow data privacy and security guidelines when using generative AI, protecting personal and institutional data"; P50.
units.anchor: Everyone must follow data privacy and security guidelines when using generative AI, protecting personal and

units.anchor: use of copyrighted materials to train generative AI models must respect these rights

units.anchor: clearly documenting the use of AI-generated content, properly attributing AI-assisted contributions in research and academic

units.why: "users must acknowledge the use of nontrivial AI-generated content and avoid plagiarism"; disclosure with a triviality threshold, P24.
units.anchor: users must acknowledge the use of nontrivial AI-generated content and avoid plagiarism

units.why: "properly citing AI-generated content in academic work"; P24.
units.anchor: properly citing AI-generated content in academic work

units.why: "It is permissible to use AI for correcting spelling and grammar and for formatting references, but not for generating new text"; permission to edit (P91) with a limit that AI may not produce new text.
units.anchor: It is permissible to use AI for correcting spelling and grammar and for formatting references,
units.fit_note: Also forbids generating new text (P19); the sentence holds both permission and limit.

units.why: "The faculty should provide clear instructions about permissible AI uses in their courses"; instructors state expectations, P09.
units.anchor: The faculty should provide clear instructions about permissible AI uses in their courses.

units.why: "specific guidance on academic integrity policies related to AI tools"; instructors tie course rules to integrity policy; P36 nearest.
units.anchor: This should include specific guidance on academic integrity policies related to AI tools.

units.why: "Biases in training data or algorithms lead to distorted and potentially harmful outcomes"; names bias and harms, P53.
units.anchor: Biases in training data or algorithms lead to distorted and potentially harmful outcomes, impacting organizational

units.anchor: may result in disciplinary action, including academic penalties or loss of access to AI tools
